source_evidence: Variable life insurance pays a specified amount of money to your family or other beneficiaries when you die.
answer: A variable life insurance death benefit is the payment made to the people you name as beneficiaries when you die. The policy’s face amount is the basis for that benefit, but the amount paid can be structured in different ways: it may equal the face amount, the face amount plus the account’s cash value, or the face amount plus premiums you contributed. Policy details matter: a policy loan may reduce the death benefit, and if the policy lapses, the beneficiary will not receive a death benefit.
